text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED - sev: SEV2
Summary: multiple model load/warmup failures for model `open_large-v2` on gpu-a node pool. Symptoms: OOM during load, CUDA allocation failures, and kernel compile timeouts causing container crashes and node flaps. Paging SRE-Oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood/1842109876

SRE-Oncall: Ack, I'm on it. @Eng Runtime please stand by. Any immediate customer-visible impact?

Jane M: Yes, seeing elevated 5xxs on hosted API routes that are pinned to `open_large-v2`. Canary traffic failing ~09:11-09:18 UTC. Repro attempt: spawn warmup job -> crash on load.

Ali R: grabbing node logs from gpu-a-13, pasting the tail here:
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:01Z] model_loader: loading open_large-v2 (version=2026-03-12)
[2026-03-14T09:12:02Z] deserializing weights... error: invalid protobuf header (0x00) at offset 0x1f
[2026-03-14T09:12:03Z] memory: trying to allocate 31.8GiB on GPU0 -> cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2026-03-14T09:12:03Z] runtime: caught std::bad_alloc during model init
[2026-03-14T09:12:04Z] cuda: cuBLAS error CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
[2026-03-14T09:12:05Z] svc: worker pid=4123 exited with code 134 (SIGABRT)
```

Kevin C (Eng Runtime): also seeing NVRTC/JIT compile timeouts in the same timeframe: kernel compile timed out after 120s (nvrtc). That combined with large preallocations during warmup -> starvation on memory. Hypothesis: warmup is preallocating full KV caches + compiling kernels concurrently, causing OOM during parallel loads.

SRE-Oncall: immediate mitigation suggestions?

Kevin C: Recommended mitigations (fast):
- disable warmup for `open_large-v2` (avoid preallocation and JIT compile spikes)
- add routing fallback -> `open_large-q4o` (smaller quantized variant) for pinned customers
- increase rolling restart grace and restart affected pods one-by-one
- temporarily set ENV `REDWOOD_SKIP_KERNEL_JIT=1` for workers to skip compile step during startup (reduces CPU/GPU memory pressure)

Jane M: Applying warmup disable now via control plane API. Command:
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.internal/v1/models/open_large-v2/config 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' 
  -d '{"warmup": false, "startup_concurrency": 1}'
```

deploy-bot: Patch applied. Configuration rollout started -> 8/12 targets updated. Rolling restart queued. :white_check_mark:

Ali R: After disabling warmup, immediate reduction in cuda allocation failures on new pods. However, several existing pods still crash during startup due to corrupted deserialization header errors seen earlier. Suspect partial object corruption on disk or a bad artifact in the deploy bundle on a subset of nodes.

SRE-Oncall: Can we identify which nodes have corrupted artifacts?

Ali R: Yes, filtering nodes with `grep -R "invalid protobuf header" /var/log/redwood/*` shows gpu-a-11 and gpu-a-13. I'm pulling the model artifact checksum now.

Kevin C: For corrupted artifact path, plan: mark those nodes unschedulable for model loads, delete local model cache, and redeploy artifact from blobstore. Command to delete cache:
```bash
ssh gpu-a-13 -- sudo rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/model-cache/open_large-v2/* && sudo systemctl restart redwood-worker
```

Jane M: Started cache clear on gpu-a-11 and gpu-a-13. Restarting worker.

deploy-bot: Worker restarts in progress (gpu-a-11, gpu-a-13). Restart results: gpu-a-11 -> success, gpu-a-13 -> pod restarted but returned OOM on first load, second attempt succeeded.

Customer Success: We're notifying affected enterprise customers that we have failover in place (routing to quantized fallback models) and are monitoring for errors. Initial CS message sent to top 3 customers who had pinned routes.

SRE-Oncall: Traffic routing update - adding route rule to divert 75% of traffic away from `open_large-v2` to `open_large-q4o` for pinned customers until root cause is resolved.

Kevin C: Additional observation: some nodes are hitting /dev/shm limits on larger batch sizes during initialization; increasing container shm to 8GiB for suspect pods has reduced OOMs. Will propose a kube patch for startup resources.

Jane M: Implemented temporary kube patch on the pool to bump `emptyDir` size for `/dev/shm` on 3 pods. Monitoring.

Ali R: Root cause investigation notes so far:
- Symptom 1: corrupted weight blob on two nodes -> deserialization error -> worker crash
- Symptom 2: concurrent JIT kernel compile + KV preallocation -> transient GPU memory starvation and cudaMalloc failures
- Symptom 3: /dev/shm too small for large batch/warmup allocations causing host oom interactions

Eng Runtime (Kevin C): Next steps for root fix:
- add a verification step during artifact download (checksum + protobuf magic validation) to fail fast and avoid corrupted loads
- serialize warmup activities (limit parallel workers doing JIT) or move compile stage to an offline build step to avoid runtime JIT spikes
- add safer fallback in loader to retry without warmup and escalate artifact repair

SRE-Oncall: Have we observed persistent customer errors after mitigations?

Jane M: 5xx rate dropped to baseline within 12 minutes of routing and warmup disable. A small number of sessions saw increased latency due to fallback model. No major data loss.

Customer Success: Customers notified; two requested dedicated postmortem and ETA for permanent fix. CS shared our current mitigation timeline and that we will provide updates.

SRE-Oncall: I'll hand this off to @Kevin C (Eng Runtime) for the long-running remediation work. Next on-call will take post-mitigation monitoring at 10:30 UTC. Handoff notes: mitigations in place, artifact replacement completed on affected nodes, routing rule to quantized models active, scale request for +2 GPUs submitted.

Kevin C: Taking ownership. I'll open an internal task to implement verification + offline kernel compile. ETA for patch: 3 business days for verification step, 2 weeks for JIT-offload work.

SRE-Oncall: Thanks team. Closing the active paging sequence. Will keep the incident thread open for updates and final postmortem. :thumbsup:

-- Incident quick timeline --
09:11 UTC - automated warmup jobs begin failing, incident-bot paged on-call
09:12 UTC - first cudaMalloc/deserialization errors observed on gpu-a-13
09:18 UTC - warmup disabled and routing fallback applied
09:30 UTC - artifact cache cleared and affected nodes restarted
09:40 UTC - 5xxs reduced to baseline, mitigations confirmed
10:10 UTC - handoff to Eng Runtime for root cause work

Impact summary: Brief service degradation for customers pinned to `open_large-v2` (increased 5xxs and some latency from fallback). No data loss, mitigations in place, prioritized follow-ups opened.

References: incident runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/internal/incidents/warmup-load-failures
